Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

Today we'll start with unit 3, so that is module 5, and we are going to learn about energy storage devices.

Key details

  • Then we learn about modern batteries like zinc air battery, lithium batteries, and specifically lithium ion battery.
  • Then we study about reserve batteries and then fuel cells.
  • principle working and efficiency of fuel cells.
  • We also look at three different types of fuel cells.
  • Hydrogen oxygen alkaline fuel cells carbon monoxide oxygen solid oxide fuel cell and methanol oxygen polynomial membrane fuel cell.
  • Then we talk about oxygen sensors.
  • And then supercapacitors and finally Ragoni plot.
  • Battery is a device which stores chemical energy and converts it into electrical energy on demand.
  • We said that they are devices which convert chemical energy stored in the reaction into electrical energy.
  • Another property of battery is that they come in variables, shapes, and sizes.
  • You can have batteries which are very tiny like the ones which are used in hearing aids, or you can have batteries which are very huge like.
  • They could weigh up to 200 tons and they are used in submarines.
  • And also the shapes of the batteries can be varied depending on the application.
  • And the third most important point about batteries is that they are portable.
  • You can carry them into space, you can use them on the land, and you can also take them underwater.
  • Three important properties of batteries which make them very useful.
  • We all know that there are a lot of applications of for batteries like in consumer goods.
  • We have mobiles, laptops, calculators, flashlights on one hand.
  • And on the other hand, we have very specific applications like in emergency lighting.
  • space vehicles, electric vehicles, and pacemakers.
  • We know that a battery is a galvanic cell, therefore we will require the two electrodes, anode and cathode.
  • What material would I choose for the anode?
  • It has to be something which undergoes oxidation very easily.
  • Therefore, we find most of the batteries they use metals as the electroactive material at anode.
  • And most commonly used materials for batteries are zinc, lead and lithium.
  • Most of the batteries now are being made with lithium.
  • And we also need a cathode where reduction takes place.
  • We know that oxidation and reduction should happen simultaneously.
  • And please remember this that a metal can never undergo reduction.
  • It can undergo oxidation.

Example or application from the lecture

  • Let us look at the various components of a battery.

Key details

  • Then MnO2 is also an oxide which is used.

  • And we can even use oxygen as the cathode active material because we know that oxy can undergo reduction easily.
  • What would serve as an electrolyte?
  • Substances which have very good ionic conductivity.
  • Ionic conductivity means we need ions which will move very easily from one electrode to the other.
  • We can have acids, we can have alkali, we can have salt solutions, we can also have molten salts.
  • And also because molten salt can produce ions which are free to move.
  • And we can also have solids which are doped oxides.
  • And then we can have polymers also which can be used as electrolytes.
  • NAFion is a polymer membrane which is used in some batteries.
  • Then we come to the last component that is a separator.
  • What is a separator?
  • It's usually an insulator which is going to separate the anode and the cathode compartment.
  • It is to prevent the anode and cathode coming in contact with each other because if that happens, there's going to be internal short circuit.
  • To separate the anode and the cathode.
  • But at the same time, it should be able to transport the ions because apart from the oxidation and reduction which is happening at the anode and cathode, respectively, this transport of ions in the through the electrolyte is very important for the battery to function.
  • Therefore the electro the separator should be able to transport the ions from anode to cathode and cathode to anode.
  • There are many types of separators which are employed based on the design of the battery.
  • But this anode active material may be in the form of a powder or a paste and therefore we need what we call as a current collector.
